For the Africa Group, the term non-treaty situation refers to circumstances where no bilateral double tax treaty agreement exists between the jurisdictions concerned, or where one or both jurisdictions are not parties to the framework convention or its protocols. In such cases, there is no common legal instrument governing the interpretation or application of cross-border tax rules between the states involved. So for instance, where both states are parties to Protocol One, that protocol itself establishes a shared legal basis for addressing disputes arising from the application of its provisions. If Nigeria, for instance, and India are both parties to Protocol One, and a 10% withholding tax rate on cross-border services is agreed, but the Nigerian tax authority applies a 15% rate to an Indian resident. The resulting disagreement constitutes a cross-border tax dispute grounded in Protocol One. In such a scenario, the dispute is not a non-treaty situation because Protocol One provides a common legal basis and an applicable legal framework. If both state parties are also parties to Protocol II, then Protocol II supplies the procedural mechanism through which the dispute should be resolved, including the map procedure or any other agreed upon modalities. Thank you.
